title: Frontend: Resizable Split Pane
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Resizable Split Pane. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. A range input labelled Left pane width stores integer percent 20..80, default 50. It controls [data-testid="left"] and right pane widths and [data-testid="ratio"] text N/100-N. Clamp all supplied changes. This native range is the pointer/keyboard resize handle.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Track the split as one value and clamp it against the container’s measured size and minimum pane widths.
alternativeApproaches: Persist the ratio rather than raw pixels and restore it safely on a narrower device.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Minimum/maximum sizes; pointer leaves handle; pointer cancellation.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
